text:
Hochwohlgebohrner Herr
Hochzuverehrender Herr Kriegs und Forst Rath.
Ich melde Euer Hochwohlgebohren hierdurch
daß der Tod des Bergraths Bernhardi
mir die Befehle, zur Reiße nach Ober¬
schlesien zuzog, und die Angelegenhei¬
ten dieser Herrschafft in Gemein¬
schafft mit denen Herrn Inspector
Kreinig und Forstmeister Reichmann
zu reguliren. Ich kann hoffen, daß es
unter der Leitung dieser Maener
besser gehen wird, da sie mir beede,

als rechtschaffene und einsichtsvolle Ge¬
schäffts-Männer bekannt sind, bin
ich in Koschentin fertig so kehre ich
nach Breslau und von da in das Reich zu¬
rück. Schlesien zu verlassen, ohne
Euer Hochwohlgebohren meinen Respect
bezeigt zu haben, würde ich mir nicht
verzeihen können. Ich bitte daher die
selben ganz gehorsamst und die Er¬
laubnis — Sie in Trąbczyn besuchen
und dort meine Aufwartung machen
zu dürfen. Ich habe auch deshalb
schon bey Sr Durchlaucht und gnädige
Erlaubnis nachgesucht, die ich zu erhalten
hoffe.
Koschentin wirdmal zu thun geben,

denn wie man rem
nimmt liegt alles dort nicht
in der besten Ordnung.
Wollten mich Hochdieselben mit einigen
Zeilem nach Koßhentin erfreuen, so
würde ich sehr glücklich seyn. Herlich
den ich bey mir habe, empfiehlt sich zu
Gnaden. Ich hanuge nur noch die Verſt.
cherung vollkommenster Verehrung auf
im der ich stets bin:
Euer Hochwohlgebohren,
Klein Althammer
d. 19. Julii
1806.
unterthänigster diener
A. Hahn

translation.en: Right Honourable Sir, Highly Honoured Sir Councillor of War and Forests. I hereby report to Your Right Honourable that the death of the mining councillor Bernhardi has brought upon me the orders to travel to Upper Silesia, and to regulate the affairs of this lordship in common with the inspector Kreinig and the master of forests Reichmann. I may hope that matters will go better under the direction of these men, since both of them are known to me,

as upright and judicious men of business. Once I have finished in Koschentin, I shall return to Breslau and from there back into the Empire. To leave Silesia without having paid my respects to Your Right Honourable is something I could not forgive myself. I therefore most obediently beg the same and for permission — to visit you in Trąbczyn and there to pay my attendance. On that account I have also already sought gracious permission from His Serene Highness, which I hope to obtain.

Koschentin will give something to do,

for, as one takes the matter, everything there is not in the best order. Should Your Highly Honoured Self be pleased to gladden me with a few lines at Koßhentin, I should be very happy. Herlich, whom I have with me, commends himself to your grace. I add only the assurance of the most perfect veneration, in which I remain always: Your Right Honourable's, Klein Althammer

the 19th of July 1806.

most humble and obedient servant

A. Hahn

text_english:
Right Honourable Sir, Highly Honoured Sir Councillor of War and Forests. I hereby report to Your Right Honourable that the death of the mining councillor Bernhardi has brought upon me the orders to travel to Upper Silesia, and to regulate the affairs of this lordship in common with the inspector Kreinig and the master of forests Reichmann. I may hope that matters will go better under the direction of these men, since both of them are known to me,

as upright and judicious men of business. Once I have finished in Koschentin, I shall return to Breslau and from there back into the Empire. To leave Silesia without having paid my respects to Your Right Honourable is something I could not forgive myself. I therefore most obediently beg the same and for permission — to visit you in Trąbczyn and there to pay my attendance. On that account I have also already sought gracious permission from His Serene Highness, which I hope to obtain.

Koschentin will give something to do,

for, as one takes the matter, everything there is not in the best order. Should Your Highly Honoured Self be pleased to gladden me with a few lines at Koßhentin, I should be very happy. Herlich, whom I have with me, commends himself to your grace. I add only the assurance of the most perfect veneration, in which I remain always: Your Right Honourable's, Klein Althammer

the 19th of July 1806.

most humble and obedient servant

A. Hahn
summary_en: Hahn reports that the death of the mining councillor Bernhardi has obliged him to travel to Upper Silesia to regulate the affairs of the lordship jointly with inspector Kreinig and master of forests Reichmann, both of whom he knows as upright and judicious men of business. Affairs at Koschentin are not in the best order and will give him work. Before leaving Silesia he asks leave to call on Triebenfeld at Trąbczyn, having already sought the Prince's permission; Herlich sends his regards.
summary_de: Hahn berichtet, daß ihn der Tod des Bergrathes Bernhardi zu einer Reise nach Oberschlesien veranlaßt habe, um die Angelegenheiten der Herrschaft gemeinschaftlich mit Inspector Kreinig und Forstmeister Reichmann zu ordnen, die er als rechtschaffene und einsichtige Geschäftsmänner kennt; in Koschentin liege nicht alles in bester Ordnung. Nach Abschluß dort wolle er über Breslau ins Reich zurück und erbittet die Erlaubnis, Triebenfeld zuvor in Trąbczyn seine Aufwartung zu machen; die Genehmigung des Fürsten sei erbeten. Er wünscht Antwort nach Koschentin; Herlich empfiehlt sich.
